attractions.name: Jemaa el-Fnaa, Marrakech
attractions.desc: Marrakech's main square shifts character completely between day and night, filled with orange-juice stalls and snake charmers by afternoon before transforming into a dense open-air food market after dark. Storytellers, musicians, and henna artists compete for space among the smoke of dozens of grills. It's been a gathering place for locals and travelers for nearly a thousand years.

attractions.name: Chefchaouen
attractions.desc: A hill town in the Rif Mountains painted almost entirely in shades of blue, a tradition with disputed origins ranging from Jewish refugee communities to simple insect-repelling practicality. Its steep, narrow lanes make for aimless, photogenic wandering rather than a checklist of sights. The surrounding mountains offer day hikes for those staying more than a night.

attractions.name: Erg Chebbi dunes, Merzouga
attractions.desc: Towering Sahara dunes reached by camel trek, with desert camps offering a night under some of the clearest skies in the country. Sunrise and sunset both transform the dune colors dramatically, from soft pink to deep orange. Sandboarding down the steepest faces is a popular addition for those staying overnight.

attractions.name: Fes el-Bali
attractions.desc: The old medina's leather tanneries and souks form one of the world's largest car-free urban areas, its narrow lanes barely wide enough for the donkeys still used to move goods. The Chouara Tannery, with its ancient stone vats of dye, remains one of the most striking and pungent sights in the city. Getting lost here is less a risk than an expectation.

attractions.name: Aït Benhaddou
attractions.desc: A fortified ksar of earthen clay buildings rising from the desert on the old caravan route between the Sahara and Marrakech, its dramatic silhouette used as a filming location for Gladiator and Game of Thrones. A handful of families still live within its walls, though most residents have moved to the newer village across the river. Climbing to the top offers wide views over the valley.

attractions.name: Majorelle Garden, Marrakech
attractions.desc: A small but densely planted botanical garden built by French painter Jacques Majorelle, later restored by fashion designer Yves Saint Laurent, its cobalt blue buildings offset by cacti and bamboo. It offers a cool, quiet retreat from Marrakech's busier streets. A small museum on-site covers Saint Laurent's connection to Morocco.

itinerary.label: Days 1–2
itinerary.title: Marrakech
itinerary.desc: Settle into the medina, visit the Bahia Palace, and get lost in the souks around Jemaa el-Fnaa.
itinerary.cost: Bahia Palace entry costs about 70 MAD (~€6.50); a hammam spa experience runs 150–400 MAD.
itinerary.food: Eat at least one dinner at the food stalls in Jemaa el-Fnaa — chaotic, cheap, and genuinely good.

itinerary.label: Day 3
itinerary.title: High Atlas day trip
itinerary.desc: Drive into the mountains to Berber villages and the Ourika Valley.
itinerary.cost: A private driver for the day costs roughly €40–60; lunch in a Berber village home runs about 100–150 MAD.
itinerary.food: Try tagine cooked the traditional way in a mountain village — often slower and richer than the city version.

itinerary.label: Days 4–5
itinerary.title: Into the Sahara
itinerary.desc: Cross the Atlas via Ouarzazate and Todra Gorge to a camp at Erg Chebbi for sunrise on the dunes.
itinerary.logistics: ~8h drive from Marrakech, best split over the day
itinerary.cost: Multi-day desert tours with a camel trek and camp run €80–150 per person, meals included.
itinerary.food: A camp dinner under the stars, usually tagine or couscous, is part of nearly every desert tour package.

itinerary.label: Days 6–7
itinerary.title: Fes
itinerary.desc: Explore the tanneries, madrasas, and the maze of the old medina.
itinerary.cost: A guided medina tour costs about €20–30 and is genuinely useful for navigating the maze; tannery viewing is often free with a small tip expected.
itinerary.food: Try pastilla, the sweet-savory pigeon or chicken pie that's a Fes specialty.

itinerary.label: Day 8
itinerary.title: Chefchaouen or Casablanca
itinerary.desc: A short detour to the blue city, or head straight to Casablanca for departure.
itinerary.cost: Chefchaouen has no major entry fees — it's mostly about wandering and photos.
itinerary.food: Try a simple bowl of harira soup at a local spot, a Moroccan staple year-round.

goodToKnow.tipping: 10% in restaurants; round up for taxis and guides
goodToKnow.safety: Generally safe; stay firm but polite with persistent guides in medinas
goodToKnow.gettingAround: Trains link major cities well; a private driver or rental car is best for the Sahara route
goodToKnow.gettingThere: Marrakech Menara Airport (RAK) is the main gateway for this route; Casablanca's Mohammed V (CMN) is Morocco's largest hub if starting or ending there instead

food.name: Tagine
food.desc: A slow-cooked stew of meat, vegetables, and warm spices, named after the cone-shaped clay pot it's cooked in.

food.name: Couscous
food.desc: Steamed semolina traditionally served on Fridays with a rich vegetable and meat broth.

food.name: Mint tea
food.desc: Sweet green tea poured from a height into small glasses, offered everywhere as a gesture of hospitality.

food.name: Pastilla
food.desc: A savory-sweet pastry pie, traditionally filled with pigeon or chicken, dusted with sugar and cinnamon.

faq.q: Do I need a visa for Morocco?
faq.a: Not for most Western passport holders (EU, UK, US, Canada, Australia) for stays up to 90 days.

faq.q: Which airport should I fly into?
faq.a: Marrakech Menara (RAK) for this route; Casablanca's Mohammed V (CMN) is Morocco's largest hub if starting or ending there instead.

faq.q: Do I need a guide for the Sahara desert trip?
faq.a: Effectively yes — this leg is normally booked as a multi-day tour with a driver and desert camp included, rather than self-driven.

faq.q: How should I handle persistent vendors in the medinas?
faq.a: A firm, polite 'no thank you' and continuing to walk works best; engaging further tends to prolong the interaction.

daysReason: 8 days covers Marrakech, the High Atlas, the Sahara, and Fes without rushing, though the driving days are long. 5–6 works if you skip the Sahara detour; 10–12 makes the driving much more relaxed.
visa: Not required for EU, UK, US, and Canadian passport holders for stays up to 90 days — always confirm current rules before booking.

attractions.name: Jemaa el-Fnaa, Marraquexe
attractions.desc: A praça principal de Marraquexe muda completamente de carácter entre o dia e a noite, cheia de bancas de sumo de laranja e encantadores de serpentes à tarde, antes de se transformar num denso mercado de comida ao ar livre depois de escurecer. Contadores de histórias, músicos e artistas de hena disputam espaço entre o fumo de dezenas de grelhadores. É um local de encontro para locais e viajantes há quase mil anos.

attractions.name: Chefchaouen
attractions.desc: Uma vila nas montanhas do Rife pintada quase inteiramente em tons de azul, uma tradição com origens disputadas, desde comunidades de refugiados judeus até uma simples utilidade prática contra insetos. As suas ruas estreitas e íngremes convidam a um passeio sem destino em vez de uma lista de pontos a visitar. As montanhas circundantes oferecem caminhadas de um dia para quem fica mais do que uma noite.

attractions.name: Dunas de Erg Chebbi, Merzouga
attractions.desc: Dunas imponentes do Saara alcançadas de camelo, com acampamentos no deserto a oferecer uma noite sob alguns dos céus mais límpidos do país. O nascer e o pôr do sol transformam dramaticamente as cores das dunas, de rosa suave a laranja intenso. Descer as faces mais íngremes de sandboard é um acrescento popular para quem pernoita.

attractions.name: Fes el-Bali
attractions.desc: As curtumes e sucos do velho medina formam uma das maiores áreas urbanas sem carros do mundo, com ruas estreitas mal dando espaço aos burros ainda usados para transportar mercadorias. A Curtume Chouara, com as suas antigas tinas de pedra e tinta, continua a ser um dos locais mais marcantes e pungentes da cidade. Perder-se aqui é menos um risco do que uma expectativa.

attractions.name: Aït Benhaddou
attractions.desc: Um ksar fortificado de construções de barro erguendo-se do deserto na antiga rota de caravanas entre o Saara e Marraquexe, com a sua silhueta dramática usada como cenário de filmagens para Gladiador e Guerra dos Tronos. Um punhado de famílias ainda vive dentro das suas muralhas, embora a maioria dos residentes se tenha mudado para a vila nova do outro lado do rio. Subir até ao topo oferece vistas amplas sobre o vale.

attractions.name: Jardim Majorelle, Marraquexe
attractions.desc: Um jardim botânico pequeno mas densamente plantado, construído pelo pintor francês Jacques Majorelle e mais tarde restaurado pelo estilista Yves Saint Laurent, com os seus edifícios azul-cobalto contrastando com cactos e bambu. Oferece um refúgio fresco e tranquilo das ruas mais movimentadas de Marraquexe. Um pequeno museu no local aborda a ligação de Saint Laurent a Marrocos.

itinerary.label: Dias 1–2
itinerary.title: Marraquexe
itinerary.desc: Instala-te na medina, visita o Palácio da Bahia e perde-te nos sucos à volta da Jemaa el-Fnaa.

itinerary.label: Dia 3
itinerary.title: Excursão ao Alto Atlas
itinerary.desc: Conduz até às montanhas para visitar vilas berberes e o Vale de Ourika.

itinerary.label: Dias 4–5
itinerary.title: Rumo ao Saara
itinerary.desc: Atravessa o Atlas via Ouarzazate e o Desfiladeiro de Todra até um acampamento em Erg Chebbi para ver o nascer do sol nas dunas.
itinerary.logistics: ~8h de carro desde Marraquexe, melhor dividido ao longo do dia

itinerary.label: Dias 6–7
itinerary.title: Fez
itinerary.desc: Explora as curtumes, madrassas e o labirinto do velho medina.

itinerary.label: Dia 8
itinerary.title: Chefchaouen ou Casablanca
itinerary.desc: Um pequeno desvio até à cidade azul, ou seguir direto para Casablanca para o regresso.

goodToKnow.tipping: 10% em restaurantes é habitual; arredonda para cima em táxis e guias
goodToKnow.safety: Geralmente seguro; mantém-te firme mas educado com guias insistentes nas medinas
goodToKnow.gettingAround: Os comboios ligam bem as principais cidades; um motorista privado ou carro alugado é melhor para a rota do Saara
goodToKnow.gettingThere: Marrakech Menara Airport (RAK) is the main gateway for this route; Casablanca's Mohammed V (CMN) is Morocco's largest hub if starting or ending there instead

food.name: Tagine
food.desc: Um guisado cozinhado lentamente com carne, legumes e especiarias quentes, com o nome do recipiente de barro em forma de cone onde é feito.

food.name: Cuscuz
food.desc: Sêmola cozida a vapor, tradicionalmente servida à sexta-feira com um caldo rico de legumes e carne.

food.name: Chá de menta
food.desc: Chá verde doce servido de uma certa altura para pequenos copos, oferecido em todo o lado como gesto de hospitalidade.

food.name: Pastilla
food.desc: Uma torta salgada e doce, tradicionalmente recheada com pombo ou frango, polvilhada com açúcar e canela.
